problems.title: Avoidance definition uses the base field

source_claim.location: p5 opening Section2; compare p2 definition and p10(III_C)
source_claim.claim: A K0-field K avoids C iff C(K0) is empty.

problems.assumptions: All characteristic-zero and smooth-geometrically-integral genus>=2 assumptions hold; the quartic partials have no common projective zero.
problems.counterexample: K0=Q, C affine x^4+y^4+1=0, smooth projective closure genus3, K=Q(zeta8). No Q-points; (zeta8,0) is a K-point.
problems.counterevidence: The abstract,p2,p10,p14 and proof already require C(K)=empty.
problems.impact: Isolated definition would admit extensions containing a forbidden point, but no actual subsequent construction step relies on that subscript.
problems.correction: Replace C(K0) by C(K); main construction remains for intended C-avoiding fields.

check.independent_reasoning: The quantified field in the printed definition is K0 while the intended exclusion is C(K)=empty. The smooth quartic X^4+Y^4+Z^4 has no rational point (including projective infinity), but has a point after adjoining an eighth root of unity. Thus the printed condition does not enforce exclusion in K. The rest of the theory explicitly uses the extension-field condition; this is a local definition-domain correction, not failure of the intended model companion.

problems.title: Computable axiomatization needs an effective base

source_claim.location: p2 Theorem1.6; p6 specialization to Q; p10 Remark2.16
source_claim.claim: Arbitrary characteristic-zero K0 yields computably axiomatized CXF in full language with every base constant.

problems.assumptions: All geometric assumptions hold; this concerns absolute computability for full L(R), not a scheme relative to a diagram.
problems.counterexample: K0=R and projective negative Fermat quartic; no real points, genus3. Any Turing enumeration mentions countably many real names. Reinterpret an unused nonzero c_r as0 in a model: all enumerated axioms preserved but c_r!=0 from R's diagram fails.
problems.counterevidence: Companion existence does not require effective language. Section2 proof locally specializes toQ; numberfield/Q applications are effective.
problems.impact: Overstates algorithmic scope; does not refute model companion or decidable nonlarge example.
problems.correction: Require computable presentation/effectively available base diagram, or explicitly say relative scheme.

check.independent_reasoning: The theorem allows uncountable K0, whereas a computable list in the full constant language mentions only countably many constants. Over R, reinterpret an unused named c_r to violate its diagram while preserving every enumerated sentence. A countable effective presentation or suitable oracle is needed. Existence is distinct from computable axiomatization; the actual decidability construction specializes Q/number fields, so no failure of those effective applications is established.

problems.title: Chow bound does not control nonpure components

source_claim.location: p4 variety convention,p5 pdeg,p7 Fact2.10; p9 graph use
source_claim.claim: One definable family contains every projective variety inP^n of bounded stated degree.

problems.assumptions: Reduced separated projective finite-type varieties are permitted; no equidimensionality convention was imposed.
problems.counterexample: InP2 over algebraically closed char0, X_N=fixedline unionN distinct off-line reducedpoints. Genericline meetsX_N once, pdeg1. A single family V_a would make V_a minusfixedline include finite fibers of allN, contrary to ACFuniformfiniteness.
problems.counterevidence: Downstream Gamma and Va under irreducibility condition are integral; needed Chow fact holds for them.
problems.impact: False auxiliary family statement outside actual irreducible usage; core graph complexity and axioms survive.
problems.correction: Restrict to pure-dimensional/irreducible varieties or bound sum of all component degrees.

check.independent_reasoning: A line together with N isolated off-line points has top-dimensional degree1 but unbounded finite zero-dimensional part. This violates the unqualified bounded-degree family assertion for non-pure varieties. Actual graph applications use integral varieties, excluding the example. The corrected equidimensional/total-component degree scope is local.

problems.title: Weil restriction product repeats factors

source_claim.claim: Split Weil restriction is product over all g in Gal(F/K).

problems.assumptions: Proper finite nonGalois extension and geometrically integral affine variety; every printed lemma assumption holds.
problems.counterexample: K=K0=Q avoids C:x^4+y^4+1=0; L=Q(cuberoot2), V=A1_L, F splittingfield ofT³-2 has GalS3 order6 (irreducible, discriminant−108 nonsquare). ResL/K A1=A3; printed sixfold product=A6.
problems.counterevidence: Correct product over3 embeddings still has transitive Gaction and no fixedfactor. Nonconstant product-to-C map depends on unique factor by4.3.
problems.impact: Invalid dimension identity in proof, but corrected transitive factor argument still establishes lemma andPAC theorem.
problems.correction: Index by Hom_K(L,F) orG/Gal(F/L), not fullG.

check.independent_reasoning: For L=Q(cuberoot2), Galois closure F has six automorphisms but only three K-embeddings of L; Res_L/K A1 has dimension3, not6. The correct split factors are indexed by G/Gal(F/L) with its natural transitive action. On that correct set the source's next unique-factor-to-K-definable-root argument is valid; the subsequent PAC use therefore has its required mathematical argument. Root actually viewed source p17 to exclude an extraction error.

problems.counterevidence: Theorem4.14 has proper algebraic extensionPAC, gives intendedCpoint and axiomIC.

problems.title: Rational function field satisfies only avoidance theory
problems.assumptions: Any KmodelsCXF; proper finiteextension exhibitsfailednecessaryaxiom; char0, curvegenus>=2 as stated.
problems.counterexample: Set t=s² with s transcendental. K(s)/K(t) degree2 proper, but C(K(s))=C(K)=empty since a nonconstant P1-to-genus>=2 map is excluded byRH and anyconstantKmap wouldgiveC(K). ThusICfails inK(t).
problems.counterevidence: K(t)modelsCXFforall is enough to invoke4.16 and get regularK'/K(t)modelsCXF, K elementaryK'.
problems.impact: False stronger intermediate assertion, not a failure of Hilbertianity or unboundedness proof after correction.
problems.correction: Write CXFforall at this step and retainregular-extensionconstruction.

check.independent_reasoning: The printed CXF assertion for K(t) lacks the universal-theory restriction; root viewed p20 and confirmed the absence. The extension K(s)/K(s^2) has degree2 and still avoids the fixed genus>=2 curve, violating the model-companion extension property.
